summary: A is preferable mainly because it introduces substantially less prohibited API surface and duplicate machinery, though neither patch faithfully implements the frozen contract.
reasons: Both patches incorrectly call Raw.Do directly from Upload instead of routing the multipart body through FilesService.Add, duplicating Add's request and response handling.
Both call a new NewFileWithFields helper rather than using internal/multipartbody.NewFile as required.
A adds one prohibited association-fields option; B adds eight public association/form APIs plus ID-validation machinery, making B a much larger contract and scope violation.
A's implementation and tests are materially smaller and easier to revise toward the required Upload -> NewFile -> Add pattern.
risks_a: WithFilesFormFields and NewFileWithFields add association behavior explicitly excluded by the contract.
The global enableBodyReplay change alters retry and body-ownership semantics outside Files.Upload.
If SeekEnd fails, enableBodyReplay still installs GetBody and may leave a seeker at an uncertain position; it also lacks the requested source-reader-error and genuinely streamed-source retry tests.
risks_b: Adds extensive prohibited association APIs, validation logic, and documentation unrelated to the exact requested convenience API.
Duplicates Add's behavior by calling Raw.Do directly.

The global request-body adoption refactor changes closing and replay semantics across Raw.Do and other services despite the contract's scope restriction; visible Upload tests also omit source-reader failure and streamed-source coverage.
